1: Fig. 1 | R2 with anchored price-identity coupling (APIC). Gated residuals produce ordered price and spread quantiles. APIC couples these outputs across publication stages. The reservation-state head combines prices, issued PV paths and completed observations to rank incremental site costs; the capacity calendar and priority recourse execute released work.
2: Fig. 2 | Workload and capacity define service slack. a, Hourly arrivals, earliest service and outstanding work around the largest episode. b, Physical service floors at 11 capacity fractions. c, Deadline violations across 19 hourly-spaced service windows; the dotted line marks the full-capacity floor.

6: Fig. 6 | Execution mechanisms across Eagle and Frontier workloads. a, Capacity-dependent service floors. b, Published DA (persistent) savings. c, Published DA (persistent) minus Published DA (myopic) savings. d, Late-work heatmaps for fixed reservations and priority recourse.
